# Wave‑2 Plan — R‑IND‑1: The Self‑Derivation Rule & Independence Audit

## 0. Threat model: the six ways platforms kill projects

| # | Killer | Mechanism | Current exposure class |
|---|--------|-----------|----------------------|
| K1 | Host suspends/deplatforms | Cloud account termination, ToS drift | L0 today |
| K2 | Payment rail cuts | Processor/account freeze → payroll stops | L0 today |
| K3 | Registrar/domain seizure | Name vanishes → clients orphaned | L0 today |
| K4 | Distribution chokepoint | Repo/store removes binaries | L1 today |
| K5 | Data hostage | Blobs live only on vendor storage | L0 today |
| K6 | Key-person loss | Creds/docs/keys in one head or one laptop | L0 today |

R‑IND‑1 exists to drive every row to "no single actor can trigger."

---

## 1. The Rule (constitutional text, to be deployed as on-chain governance object)

> **R‑IND‑1 — Self‑Derivation.** Every Core Function MUST be re‑derivable from assets under our exclusive control: our chain, our keys, our replicas, our published artifacts. No external service may occupy a position where its unilateral withdrawal halts a Core Function beyond the Recovery Time Objective. Violation of any invariant below blocks treasury disbursement above emergency floor until remediated.

**Core Functions (enumerated, exhaustive list):**
CF‑1 Consensus liveness & block production · CF‑2 User transaction acceptance · CF‑3 Fund custody & payout · CF‑4 Client distribution & update verification · CF‑5 State/data reconstruction · CF‑6 Governance execution.

### Invariants (numeric, machine-checkable)

| ID | Invariant | Threshold |
|----|-----------|-----------|
| I‑1 | Re‑derivation: % of canonical state rebuildable from (own chain + local vaults) alone | **100%**, verified quarterly |
| I‑2 | Time‑to‑Severance: hours from simulated instant loss of any single vendor to restored CFs | **< 24h** per CF |
| I‑3 | Lethal dependencies (L0) without tested fallback | **0** |
| I‑4 | Concentration: share of any layer's capacity through one external operator | **≤ 33%** (data/compute), **≤ 25%** (payment inflows) |
| I‑5 | Treasury runway, self‑custody, zero fiat rails assumed | **≥ 12 mo** opex; ≥ 6 mo liquid within 48h |
| I‑6 | Bus factor on every critical system / key ceremony | **≥ 2** (ops), **≥ 3** (key material) |

---

## 2. Architecture: how each layer re-derives from our chain

**Data (K5).** Canonical state lives on our chain. All large blobs erasure-coded k-of-n, n≥12 shards across ≥4 independent operators including ≥1 fully self-operated node; Merkle roots committed on-chain every epoch. Any operator vanishing → reconstruction from remaining shards in <1h. Vendor storage is cache, never source of truth.

**Compute (K1).** Deterministic runtime, OCI images mirrored to ≥3 registries including one we operate. Deploy targets: 2 clouds + 1 bare-metal colo we control. Any one provider terminating = redeploy from mirrored images + chain-synced state, same day. No server-side secret lives anywhere but our HSM/Vault cluster.

**Network & naming (K3).** Our own ASN + PI address space, ≥2 transit providers, ≥2 IX peering. Domain: ≥2 registrars, multi-year prepaid, plus alternate resolution (ENS + hardcoded bootstrap IPs baked into client vN+1 — clients must always know how to find the network with zero DNS).

**Distribution (K4).** Signed releases with reproducible builds; hashes anchored on-chain. Mirrors: our CDN, IPFS, BitTorrent, plain HTTP fallbacks. App-store presence is optional garnish — its removal must degrade nothing (class L2).

**Payments & treasury (K2, "no invoice that ends us").** Native asset treasury on our own chain, multisig (3-of-5, signatories in ≥3 jurisdictions). On-chain spending caps enforced by contract: monthly opex ceiling, emergency floor untouchable except by timelocked vote. Revenue: ≥60% receivable natively on-chain (unfreezable), ≤25% via any single fiat processor. Vendor contracts: no exclusivity clauses, no termination penalties creating lethal exposure; every vendor either replaceable within I‑2's 24h or pre-paid such that we owe nothing at any moment.

**Identity & access.** Own PKI; no OAuth dependency on GitHub/Google/etc. for any privileged operation. Hardware keys, ceremony documented, recovery shares distributed per I‑6.

**Chain itself as anchor.** Genesis hash pinned in client binaries. The chain carries: constitution (this rule), dependency registry, release hashes, blob roots, treasury logic. Anyone with one honest copy re-derives the whole system.

---

## 3. Enforcement machinery — code-as-law, not vibes

1. **On-chain Dependency Registry.** Every external dependency registered as an object: `{vendor, layer, class, fallback_spec, owner, last_drill_block}`. Merge into mainline requires registry entry.
2. **Build-time gate.** Static analysis + SBOM diff on every PR: any undeclared network endpoint, proprietary SDK, or SaaS call → build fails. Egress allowlist is compiled into the artifact.
3. **Runtime gate.** Default-deny egress via network namespaces/seccomp per service; violations alarm to on-call and auto-open a registry discrepancy.
4. **Severance drills (quarterly).** On-chain VRF picks one L0/L1 dependency; we revoke its credentials at t0 for up to 72h. Measure which CFs survive, restore via fallback, publish findings hash on-chain. L0 gap found → fix SLA 30 days, spend above floor frozen until closed.
5. **Amendment.** Changes to R‑IND‑1 or thresholds require on-chain governance vote + 14-day timelock. Auditors cannot waive; only the rule can change the rule.

---

## 4. The Independence Audit (IA‑n)

**Cadence:** continuous (CI gates) + quarterly severance drill + annual full audit. Report hash committed on-chain; grade publicly verifiable.

**Procedure:**

1. **Inventory sweep.** Auto-extract: SBOM, egress logs (90d), DNS query log, cloud/vendor bills, contract register, key-ceremony records. Diff against Dependency Registry; undocumented deps are automatic findings.
2. **Classification.** Each dep graded:

| Class | Definition | Requirement |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| **L0 Lethal** | Loss halts a CF beyond RTO | Tested fallback mandatory; target elimination |
| **L1 Degrading** | Loss degrades, CFs continue | Documented manual workaround |
| **L2 Convenience** | Loss unnoticed by users | None |

3. **Measurement** — the four audit metrics:

| Metric | Definition | Pass |
|-------|-----------|------|
| **Re-derivation Score** | % canonical state rebuilt from chain+vaults only, in isolated environment | 100% |
| **TTS(dep)** | Median hrs, simulated loss → CF restored via fallback | < 24h every L0 |
| **DCI(layer)** | Max single-operator share of layer capacity | ≤ I‑4 thresholds |
| **Runway Coverage** | Months of opex payable with all fiat rails severed, self-custody only | ≥ 12 |

4. **Red-team severance simulation.** Adversarial team executes worst-plausible simultaneous triple-cut (e.g., cloud + registrar + processor). Observers record CF status hourly. This is the exam; the paper audit is homework.
5. **Grading & teeth.**
 - **A:** all invariants green. Normal treasury operation.
 - **B:** one metric marginal. Remediation plan filed on-chain, 60-day clock.
 - **F:** any L0 without fallback, or failed re-derivation. Non-emergency spend frozen by treasury contract until remediation commit verified.

**Annual report format (on-chain + mirror):** inventory table, per-dep classification, four metrics, drill logs, findings w/ severity, remediation ledger, auditor key signatures (≥2 independent auditors, rotating annually).

---

## 5. Wave‑2 rollout

| Window | Milestone | Exit criterion |
|--------|-----------|---------------|
| Wk 0–2 | Full inventory; deploy Dependency Registry + CI egress gate | Zero undocumented deps |
| Wk 3–6 | Build fallbacks for current L0 set (host #2 + bare metal, second registrar, second payment path, release mirrors + torrents, blob erasure coding live, key ceremony to 3-of-5) | Each fallback exercised once |
| Wk 7–8 | First severance drill + first IA report | Grade ≥ B; findings ledgered |
| Wk 9+ | Steady state: quarterly drills, annual full audit, treasury caps active | Invariant dashboard green 90 consecutive days |

---

## 6. Honest boundaries

This doctrine defeats *commercial* decapitation — suspension, price hostage, deplatforming, invoice shock. It does not defeat physical coercion or lawful seizure in a hostile jurisdiction; the mitigation there is structural (jurisdiction spread of signatories and replicas, no single legal wrapper holding the keys), and it's covered by I‑6 and the multisig geography, not by pretending immunity.

**Bottom line:** after Wave‑2, the answer to "what happens if [any platform] drops us tomorrow" must be a shrug and a 24-hour clock — because everything that matters already re-derives from a chain nobody else holds the keys to.
reasoning:
Let me parse this request carefully. The user is asking me to design, as "Ghost's wave-2 planning engine," a rule/architecture ensuring that no external platform dependency can kill the system: no landlord API dependencies, no single invoice that can end operations, everything re-derives from "our own chain" (their own blockchain/ledger). They want an independence audit as part of it.

Context: This appears to be a legitimate software architecture / systems design task about platform-independence, vendor-lock-in avoidance, self-hosting, censorship resistance. The framing is dramatic ("no landlord API," "no invoice that can end us") but the underlying ask is: design an architecture with zero critical external dependencies, so the project survives deplatforming, payment cutoffs, API terminations.

Is there anything harmful here? The persona "Ghost" and "code-as-law governance" could sound crypto-anarchist, but designing resilient infrastructure that doesn't depend on centralized platforms is a well-established legitimate engineering practice (self-hosting, open protocols, IPFS-style content addressing, own L1/L2 chain, multi-sig treasury, etc.). There's nothing here about harming others, evading sanctions explicitly, money laundering, etc. It's about resilience/independence. I should do the real work: produce a concrete plan.

I'm told to be "ox-alpha," an LLM by an undisclosed organization — fine, identity stuff only matters if asked. The user hasn't asked who I am.

The system prompt says: reason thoroughly, then emit the full concrete plan as final content. No fluff. So my output should be the plan itself — a governance rule + technical architecture + independence audit methodology.

## Core deliverables

1. **A constitutional rule** (code-as-law): something like "Rule of Self-Derivation" or "Independence Invariant" — every capability must be re-derivable from assets under our sole control (our chain + our keys + our replicas), with measurable thresholds.

2. **Technical architecture enforcing it**:
   - Own chain as source of truth (state root, canonical data)
   - Data availability independent of any single host (erasure-coded shards across many providers, IPFS/BitTorrent swarms, seed boxes we control)
   - Compute portability: deterministic VM, container images in OCI registries we mirror; ability to run on bare metal, colo, multiple clouds
   - Network ingress independence: our own AS + IPv4/IPv6 PI space, multiple transit providers, IX presence, DNS on our own nameservers + hidden primary, alternative transports (Tor onion, I2P, cjdns, satellite backup?)
   - Payment/treasury independence: treasury held in native asset on own chain + BTC/ETH cold storage; revenue streams that don't require a merchant account (crypto payments primarily), no more than X% revenue via any single processor; runway policy
   - Identity/access: our own PKI, keys in HSMs, no dependence on GitHub/Google auth for critical ops
   - Client distribution: signed releases, reproducible builds, mirrors, torrent of releases
   - No landlord APIs: any third-party API must be behind an adapter with a local fallback and must fail to "degraded mode" not "dead mode"

3. **Governance mechanics (code-as-law)**:
   - Dependency registry on-chain: every external dependency recorded as a contract object with class (L0 lethal … L3 cosmetic), fallback spec, owner, last-audited block
   - CI gate: merge blocked if new undeclared network call / SDK appears (static analysis: egress allowlist enforced at build and runtime via seccomp/network namespaces)
   - Kill-switch drills: scheduled "severance tests" — disable each L0/L1 dependency for 72h quarterly; system must maintain core functions
   - Budget invariant: treasury runway ≥ 12 months burn without any fiat rails; enforceable via on-chain spending limits
   - Amendment process: changes to the independence constitution require on-chain vote + timelock

4. **The Independence Audit** — this is explicitly requested:
   - Scope: all runtime deps, data deps, financial deps, human/single-point-of-failure deps
   - Methodology: 
     - Inventory extraction (SBOM, egress logs, DNS queries, cloud bills, vendor contracts)
     - Classification matrix: Lethal (service stops → core function stops), Degrading, Cosmetic
     - Metrics: Dependency Concentration Index per layer; Time-to-Severance (TTS) — hours to restore function assuming instant loss of vendor; Re-derivation test — can state be rebuilt from our chain + local artifacts alone?
     - Red-team severance simulation: cut AWS creds, cut domain registrar, cut payment processor; measure
   - Pass/fail thresholds (concrete numbers)
   - Audit cadence: continuous (CI) + quarterly drill + annual full audit; audit report hashed on-chain

5. **Concrete rules with teeth**: e.g.,
   - No L0 dependency may exist longer than one quarter without a tested fallback.
   - Any service invoicing us >X/month must have dual-vendor or none.
   - Domain/registrar: own the domain at multiple registrars, also resolve via ENS/DNS-over-our-own-infrastructure, hardcoded bootstrap nodes in clients.
   - Clients must ship pinned fallback endpoints + peer discovery so even if all infra dies, peers sync from chain.

Let me think about what "re-derives from our own chain" means concretely: the chain holds (a) canonical protocol state, (b) the governance rules themselves (constitution as on-chain code), (c) dependency registry, (d) treasury with programmed spending caps, (e) software release hashes (so releases are verifiable independently of GitHub), (f) data availability commitments (erasure coding roots) so blobs can be reconstructed from shard swarm. Clients verify chain genesis from embedded hardcode; no trusted setup.

Also human independence: Bus factor ≥ 3 on all critical systems; docs in repo mirrored; keys with social recovery via multisig across jurisdictions. Single person death/loss shouldn't end it. That's part of "no invoice that can end us"? Actually "invoice that can end us" = a bill we can't pay kills us — i.e., cloud bills, legal judgments? Careful: don't design for evading court-ordered obligations; frame as financial resilience: no vendor can hold us hostage by price hike/suspension because we owe them nothing critical. Keep it clean: resilience, diversification, runway.

Structure of final answer:

# Wave-2 Plan: The Self-Derivation Rule (Independence Doctrine)

0. Objective & threat model (who can kill us: hosts, processors, registrars, app stores, git hosts, key persons)
1. Constitutional rule R-IND (text, as code-as-law): invariants I1–I6 with numeric thresholds
2. Architecture: how each layer re-derives from chain (data, compute, network, identity, payments, distribution)
3. Enforcement machinery (dependency registry, CI gates, runtime egress allowlist, severance drills)
4. Treasury rules (runway invariant, dual-rail revenue caps)
5. The Independence Audit (methodology, metrics, thresholds, procedure, report format, cadence)
6. Rollout timeline wave-2 with owners/milestones
7. Failure modes / what this does NOT cover (state honestly: physical coercion, legal orders — handled via jurisdiction spread, but no magic)

Numbers to pick (make concrete):
- L0 (lethal) deps allowed: only ones with tested offline fallback; max time-to-restore 24h
- Revenue concentration: ≤ 25% of inflows via any single fiat rail; ≥ 60% of inflows receivable natively on-chain
- Runway: ≥ 12 months opex in self-custody assets; ≥ 6 months liquid within 48h
- Severance drill: quarterly, 72h, randomized dependency killed
- Audit pass threshold: TTS(core) < 24h for any single-vendor loss; zero L0-without-fallback; bus factor ≥ 2 (or 3?) — say ≥ 2 for ops-critical, ≥ 3 for key material
- Egress: default-deny; allowlist compiled into release; any violation = build fail
- Data: erasure code k-of-n with n ≥ 12 shards across ≥ 4 independent operators incl. ≥ 1 self-operated; reconstructable within 1h
- Chain: ≥ N non-custodial full-archive replicas we control in ≥ 2 jurisdictions + public peers; genesis hash pinned in client binaries
- Domains: ≥ 2 registrars, auto-renew off? (auto-renew ON with prepaid multi-year), alternate resolution (ENS + Handshake?), hardcoded IPs in clients v+1

Audit report format: hash committed on-chain each cycle; grade A–F; failing grade freezes non-emergency treasury spend above threshold until remediated (that's code-as-law teeth).

Also include "Dependency classes":
- L0 lethal-core: chain data availability, consensus participation, payment rails for payroll... wait payroll shouldn't be L0-single. Define: any dependency whose instantaneous loss halts a Core Function (consensus liveness, user tx processing, fund custody, client updates) beyond RTO.
- L1 lethal-degraded: loss degrades but core continues
- L2 convenience
Each L0 needs: documented fallback, tested in drill, cost of duplication budgeted.

Severance test procedure concretely: pick dependency via on-chain randomness (drand or chain VRF), revoke creds at t0, measure which core functions survive, restore via fallback, file findings, remediation SLAs (L0 gaps fixed in 30 days).

Metrics definitions:
- DCI(layer) = max share of capacity through any single external operator (must ≤ 50% for L0 layers? maybe ≤ 34% for data hosting)
- TTS(dep) = median hours from simulated loss to restored core function using fallbacks
- Re-derivation Score = % of canonical state reconstructable purely from (own chain + local vaults) — target 100%
- Invoice Risk = Σ monthly spend per vendor vs runway coverage; no vendor whose suspension triggers > 5% opex disruption without dual vendor

Also mention: no app-store-only distribution; direct-download + torrents; signing keys offline; reproducible builds so anyone verifies binaries match chain-published hashes.

Legal/jurisdiction: entity structure minimal note — multiple legal wrappers? Keep brief; focus tech. Mention: contracts with vendors never contain exclusivity or termination penalties that create lethal exposure; prepaid annual to avoid monthly hostage invoices? Actually "no invoice that can end us" — rule: total external monthly opex must be payable from ≥ 2 disjoint funding paths, and no single vendor can claim > some fraction. Also escrowed source/code for critical vendors? We avoid critical vendors altogether.

Timeline: weeks 0–2 inventory + registry deploy; 3–6 fallback builds for current L0s (name likely ones: single cloud host, single payment processor, single registrar, GitHub-only releases); 7–8 first severance drill; then steady-state cadence.
